column97:
08/Apr/08 10:34 PM;557058:c714f0f0-b42d-45c7-be2f-d002135599e4;This is a modification of the acts_as_authentable plugin. It handles password
encryption, authentication, identification of current users and admins, login status,
and remember_me. 

Key features:

To enable authentication, puts "acts_as_authentable" in the model; to disable extra
features (remember_me, for example), use "acts_as_authentable(false)". (There's
probably a more intuitive way to set that up.) Then run "script/generate authentable
yourmodelname" to create a migration to add columns to the model. For regular models,
those are: login, email, salt, crypted_password, remember_token,
remember_token_expires_at, activation_code, and activated_at. If the model name
contains the word "admin", it leaves off the last four, and just gives you: login,
email, salt, and crypted_password. 

Validations and authentication/encryption methods are in authentable_entity.rb. 

Methods related to the current session (current_user, logged_in?, etc.) are in
user_authentication.rb and admin_authentication.rb. 

Remember me/forget me methods are in session_persistence.rb. 

You should be able to access current_user, current_admin, logged_in?, and
logged_in_as_admin? from other controllers and views. You can also use login_required
and admin_only as filters. The user_logout_required and admin_logout_required filters
are to prevent people with multiple accounts from having overlapping logins; those
should include a redirect to a logical place. 

Activation emails and methods live outside the plugin right now.

column98:
31/Aug/08 12:22 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;As of revision 511:

Via acts_as_authentable we now have validation for:
- login length (3-40 characters)
- password length (6-40 characters)
- email length (3-100 characters)
- uniqueness of login and email

We also have validation for: 
Users:
- login format: begin and end with a letter or number, may contain only letters,
numbers, and underscores. 
- validity of email address (should match requirements and also check for valid mail
server at domain)
- acceptance of Terms of Service
- confirmation of age over 13

Pseuds:
- pseuds must have a name
- name must have at least one letter or number in it
- name may contain only letters, numbers, spaces, underscores, and dashes
- name cannot be more than 40 characters long

Works:
- title, summary, and notes must be between the min/max values specified in the
config (currently 255, 1250, and 2500 characters respectively). 
- title must be present.

Chapter: 
- title, summary, and notes must be between the min/max values specified in the
config (same as for Works)
- content must be present and at least 10 letters and no more than 500,000 letters.

External Work: 
- title and summary must be between min/max values specified in config, and title
must be present.

Bookmark: 
- notes must be no more than max value specified in config. 

Comment validation is not presently working, but this is a separate problem, see
issue 290. - **Status changed**: `FixedAndVerified`

column1: Improvements to translation interface
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 28
Alas, click-to-globalize has some issues we've uncovered now we've used it
for a while. It stores strings in the session, making it too large to use
cookie storage, and storing session info in the db is not great. 

So instead, we will be using just the single-page translation mechanism.
However, we want to get some of the advantages of click-to-globalize into
this page instead. 

Goals: 
* Strings should have a link to the page they come from.
* Strings that have to be "broken up" because they contain links in context
should be kept together and ideally presented as a single string for
translation. 
* Strings should be nicely sorted and stay in order. 
* If possible, a bit of before/after context would be included around the
strings to translate. 
* When strings are input, they should be sanitized to strip all HTML tags.
Translations should only contain text.
* We should have in-place-editing enabled for those translators with
Javascript.

This may require expanding the ViewTranslations object that is part of
Globalize.

column108:
21/Apr/24 3:49 AM;557058:baa5f297-c116-4036-bbf1-109f8a7e50a7;I looked into the Phrase In-Context Editor (ICE). There is a [Ruby gem|https://rubygems.org/gems/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby] available. In fact, an older version of the gem is already installed and configured for the archive. However, it most likely wasn’t activated or used in a while: It’s broken on the homepage of the archive since at least Ruby 3.0.

I would target the new ICE (linked below by Sarken), so the gem needs to be updated to at least version 2.0.0 and newly configured. There are a few roadblocks for this:

* -Version 2.0.0 of the gem requires Ruby 3.2. The archive currently uses Ruby 3.1. I opened a PR for the gem to- [-support Ruby 3.1-|https://github.com/phrase/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/pull/74]-.- Merged and released as gem version 2.1.1.
* Parts of the gem are not or only improperly updated to handle the [Ruby 3.0 change to positional and keyword arguments|https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2019/12/12/separation-of-positional-and-keyword-arguments-in-ruby-3-0/]. This was already [monkeypatched once by us|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4439], and there is another instance of this issue [here|https://github.com/phrase/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/blob/8f87ed8a5a97512431b6c478ece4703c3bc5588c/lib/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/delegate/i18n_delegate.rb#L27]. This causes the crash on the archive homepage in the currently installed version of the gem. This crash is in [number_with_delimiter|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/NumberHelper.html#method-i-number_with_delimiter], which suggest to me that Phrase may be overeager in inserting itself into translation functions, but I did not investigate further.
* Phrase inserts itself into Faker generators. This is not a problem for the usual website translations because Faker is not used during normal operation. However, the mailer previews use Faker to generate email addresses and text used in the emails. Phrase replaces these with its placeholder strings, which leads to issues similar to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6386|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6386|smart-link] . So Phrase should be prevented from inserting itself into the generators, because they shouldn’t show up in the ICE either.
* [The docs|https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784095916188-In-Context-Editor-Strings] recommend a separate staging environment. I would also recommend it because enabling the ICE appears to interfere with normal site function.

The good things:

* I manually patched/worked around the issues above and got the ICE to work locally.
* Because I am not AD&T nor Translation, I couldn’t log into Phrase to activate the editor. However, even without logging in, it was clear that the gem was working, because the placeholders for the ICE were used everywhere the translation method was used and showed the correct keys.
* The ICE also works inside mailer previews.
column109:
12/May/24 4:18 AM;557058:baa5f297-c116-4036-bbf1-109f8a7e50a7;An update on the state of the phrase in context editor Ruby gem:

* As edited into the previous comment, the gem can now be used with Ruby 3.1.
* Someone else opened a PR in phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby to fix the args/kwargs issue that [tickinginstant monkeypatched|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4439]: [https://github.com/phrase/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/pull/78|https://github.com/phrase/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/pull/78|smart-link] Update: Merged, released.
* I opened a PR in phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby to fix the second args/kwargs issue: [https://github.com/phrase/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/pull/79|https://github.com/phrase/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/pull/79|smart-link] Update: Merged, released.
* Both problems with the gem inserting itself into number_with_delimiter and into Faker generators could be fixed by making the gem ignore translation calls using specific keys ({{number.*}} and {{faker.*}} respectively). This was possible in the old ICE with an {{ignored_keys}} config option, however the new ICE does not support this configuration. I opened an [issue requesting the option|https://github.com/phrase/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/issues/80], the response was that they don’t think they will get to it anytime soon. However, the code for this should be pretty simple. So after the two bugs are fixed, a PR could be made to get the option added, or we could monkeypatch the gem to add it. Update: [PR opened|https://github.com/phrase/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/pull/82]

27/Jun/24 12:36 PM;557058:baa5f297-c116-4036-bbf1-109f8a7e50a7;Another month, another update. My last PR to the gem was merged and the In-context editor now works out of the box! I’ve configured its latest version on this branch: [https://github.com/Bilka2/otwarchive/tree/AO3-105-phrase-in-context-editor|https://github.com/Bilka2/otwarchive/tree/AO3-105-phrase-in-context-editor|smart-link]

[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/commit/2e3c45d094b7df716d21c63e05fff18a8d997ef5|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/commit/2e3c45d094b7df716d21c63e05fff18a8d997ef5|smart-link]  fixes the main page and parts of the navigation bar, however the dropdown content (dropdown-menu) in the navigation bars also needs a fix.

column1: language drop-down list inaccessible to screen readers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 118
Revision 200
The combo box that lists available languages for translation needs to be 
activated by a button, rather than dynamically as the user scrolls. The 
problem is that when a screen reader user hits enter on the box to enter 
forms mode which allows interaction with form elements, and then hits down 
arrow to scroll, the page automatically reloads at the next listed option. 
The user can't just scroll through all the options and pick one, she has 
to load each and every one, or get lucky and hit the first letter of her 
choice and hope it's the first one listed starting with that letter.
This goes for all drop-down lists.
column98:
18/May/08 3:34 PM;557058:3785a99a-fc51-48ca-849f-1bb76dd2deb1;Button activation is already available if the user has javascript turned off -
obviously this does not resolve the issue for those using screenreaders. The on-click
interface could be removed, or a new solution adopted. Some options discussed in the
coding room (see transcript
https://fanarchive.campfirenow.com/room/136857/transcript/2008/05/18 ) but the right
way forward with this probably needs to be determined by design.
column100: 25/May/08 5:52 AM;557058:3785a99a-fc51-48ca-849f-1bb76dd2deb1;- **Status changed**: `Assigned`
column101:
02/Jun/08 10:52 AM;557058:3785a99a-fc51-48ca-849f-1bb76dd2deb1;Solution implemented with revision 269.

As discussed with black_samvara and the design team, a javascrpt solution has been
implemented for this issue which overrides default browser behaviour for this menu.
This gives the following behavior:

NAVIGATING BY KEYBOARD
User can tab into and out of the menu, without triggering a change.
User can explore all the options in the menu using up an down keys, without
triggering a change.
User can leave the menu without triggering a change by pressing escape or tab.
User can submit a change by selecting an option with the arrow keys and pressing 'enter'.

NAVIGATING BY MOUSE (no change to how it was before)
User can submit a change by clicking on the language they want to change to.
User can leave the menu without submitting a change by clicking outside the menu.

Would welcome input from testers on whether this is a good solution for keyboard
navigation, and whether any of the key behaviours are counter-intuitive. It would
also be helpful if someone who is used to using a screenreader could try it out.- **Status changed**: `FixedButUnverified`

column104:
14/Jun/08 3:04 AM;557058:327d6059-0150-4fe5-8791-0d5e6025a597;Okay, here's what I found out after looking further into this:

Technical stuff:

The wrong display came about because we escaped all HTML in titles (on the story and
preview page), even if it was already escaped. The story list doesn't escape, so it
was always displayed correctly there.

The different behavior between post and edit can be explained because when posting
we
immediately save the input of the user, so the entities are stored as entities. For
editing however we store them in the preview in hidden fields which are semi-escaped,
meaning that only the parts that aren't already escaped get escaped. When we read the
field, we get the unescaped version of everything, which is where the entity gets
turned into a non-entity (the apparent "fix").

I think we should change it so that both posting and updating will result in
unescaped content in the DB.

My question for design:

I just checked the Wireframes 200.3.pdf (is that the latest version?). It says that
when posting there is a limited set of HTML available, but it didn't say which set.
I
also didn't see that we're limiting this in the code right now (except for stripping
script and forms, which the sanitize does).

For the titles we don't say anything (they might have the same tag restrictions or
more).

So my question would be, have we decided which tags exactly we want to allow in the
various fields?

column98:
12/Jun/08 9:16 PM;557058:be6d5da9-c318-4a37-90a3-f06f5f84c0eb;has_many_polymorphs does not allow self-referential associations where the name of the
association and the name of the model are the same. e.g.

tag.tags << Tag.create

They recommend
tag.taggers << Tag.create
but I felt
work.taggers was less desirable than work.tags

so I used
work.tags << Label.create
which also allows
label.tags << Label.create

I decided to go with tagging the tags, rather than creating the long and varied list
of self-referential relationships and models that the roadmap called for.

Thus, instead of
belongs_to :definition, :as => :synonym
you can create a definition tag (meta == 'canonical') which can be applied to a label.

instead of
belongs_to :parent, :class_name => :tag, :as => :child
you can create a definition tag  (meta == 'parent') which can be applied to a label.

instead of 
TagCategory model: id, name, description, is_official
you create a tag with meta == 'official' - the name of the tag is the category name

I feel this is the best way to implement the functionality which was required by the
roadmap. I've checked in my work in r294 so you can see how it works. If you 
don't like it, and want me to implement the roadmap exactly as defined, let me know
and I'll back it all out.

column1: Enhancement: Automatic tagging from content
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 158
We want to process the content of stories to automatically suggest
appropriate tags, including characters, pairings, fandom. 

Initial approach: search new stories for the presence of words matching the
string of Tag objects in the Character TagCategory, then use the
relationships those tags have to tags in the Fandom and Pairing
TagCategories to generate a set of possible tags. 

This should probably be done as a function on Work that will return an
array of Tag objects, and optionally take a particular TagCategory to limit
the types of tags returned. 

Later expansions could also generate suggested tags from: 

- tags on the user's other stories
- commonly-grouped tags in the archive
- tags on similar stories in the archive (this would first require some way
to measure similarity between stories a la Google's "search for similar
pages" feature)
column98:
27/Sep/08 5:51 PM;557058:b752fd71-6f71-4898-b3c0-e619db03518f;In practice, this automation appears to limit the author's choice as to the
presentation of both oevre and individual stories, while adding little to readers'
customization ability, which is better served in the search and filtering
functionalities in any event.

Example: I upload a story in which I enter character names in the Character field in
the order of their importance to the story [Missouri Moseley, Bobby Singer, Sam
Winchester]. The engine reprioritizes them according to some other schema that
consequently misclassifies the story as it's presented to the casual browser [Sam
Winchester, Bobby Singer, Missouri Moseley].

Example: My entry in the "People" listing is accompanied by a set of automatically
generated tags that appear to label me as a Het Alias writer. It's true that most of
the stories I've uploaded to date are classified het and sourced in the Alias fandom
-- but that isn't how I'd prefer to present myself for the casual browser: at present
I'm a Gen SPN TSCC writer. The Alias work isn't my most recent nor my best, in spite
of being the majority of my stories at present. 

Why not let the author/artist choose which values to list for public consumption?
Readers have ample opportunity to expand or otherwise qualify that information with
recs, tags, bookmarks, and other filtering that's also available to archive users,
as
the individual sees fit.

In short, I'd like to see the author/artist allowed maximum choice in the
presentation of her work to both searchers and casual browsers. The archive is
clearly being set up to offer a myriad of tools for reader access/customization that
need not impinge on that initial self-presentation.

When listing works (currently in view all works, eventually on
search/browse results), we should display a summary of the tags on each work. 

To generate the summary: 
- Combine tags from the author with tags from any bookmarkers that the user
is subscribed to.
- To make the list display nicely, we need to:
-- winnow down the list to a limited number of tags: prioritize tags by how
often a given tag was used on the story, how popular the tag is in the
archive; as fallback and for initial pass, choose tags randomly 
-- abbreviate very long tags -- could do something like <abbr title="full
string value of tag">[first eight letters of tag]...</abbr>. Or possibly
using Tag Relationships, take the shortest "synonym" of a tag to display,
with the longest version as the full value?

- Eventually: if browsing/searching by a set of tags, REMOVE those tags
from the summary since they will be on every work in the results.

13/Aug/16 6:20 PM;557058:77351d0c-19f2-456d-8c3f-39bc145cb6dd;Extra fun facts:

1) If a comment marked as spam has children, they will become invisible to anyone but admins along with the spam comment.  (When viewed as admin, they have a "Spam" button rather than "Not Spam", so they're presumably not being marked as spam.) They are still included in the overall comment count.

2) Deleting the parent marked as spam causes the child comment to re-appear, with "(Previous comment deleted.)" as a placeholder parent.  The comment count is now correct for the number of visible comments.

It seems undesirable for someone's non-spam response to be automatically hidden when a comment is hidden as spam; if the response is considered irrelevant or confusing (by the work creator, comment leaver, or admin) with the spam gone, it can always be deleted. Updated issue title to reflect this concern.

column115:
02/May/17 2:34 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Here are some detailed steps for checking the comment counts, if they would be useful:

# Create a work with many comments, at least some of which are guest comments.
# Mark one of the guest comments as spam.
# View the number of comments on the work blurb (e.g. by going to the author's works page).
# View the number of comments on the work header (by clicking on the work and looking at the "Stats:" field at the top of the page).
# View the number of comments in the work's footer (by clicking on the work and scrolling down to "Comments (#)").

All three of those numbers should agree with each other, and they should all reflect the fact that the number of visible comments has decreased.
column116:
07/Oct/17 4:17 PM;557058:77351d0c-19f2-456d-8c3f-39bc145cb6dd;Created a work with three "spam" guest comments - one parent, one reply, one by itself - and four non-spam comments

column1: Error message system - design [ERRORS]
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 185
What archive revision are you testing on? r313

We need a consistent error message system design, and language for a set of
common error messages. Notes from 6/21 meeting:

Common rails error types
the "flash" warnings that appear at the top of the page
errors in-line right above the text
live validations -- errors that appear as you type

The "flash" error messages currently come in three varieties: failure
(meaning something didn't happen), warning (something happened but possibly
not everything/not what you wanted), and information (generally just
confirming that what you wanted happened)

failure is currently red, skull&crossbones, warning is yellow exclamation
point, info is blue lightbulb

We like some combination of the flash error message at the top plus inline
errors, because inline errors can sometimes be hard to spot -- it just
looks like the page reloaded for no reason

column1: Word Count: Tags
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 254
We want to make it easy to find/browse stories by length, so in addition to
listing the exact word count on the story, we want to use tags for
searching and browsing. We'll need: 1) a tag category for length (which
doesn't show up on the work form!) and 2) code to automatically apply the
right length tag to a work whenever it's saved.

The current proposed tags and their corresponding lengths (in words):

drabble: <=100
short: <3000
medium: <15000
long: <30000
novel: >30000
column97:
28/Aug/08 10:36 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;I'm going to take a stab at this in a slightly different direction; this solution
would unfortunately require people to know a nonstandard set of definitions for these
words that may not match their intuitive expectations. Also we don't want to be
auto-applying a tag, IMO -- the wordcount info is already available, and is
changeable over the life of a story, so effectively duplicating the info in the db
is
not ideal. 

It would be more useful IMO to build a separate wordcount option to search/browse
using numbers (and ideally allow advanced users to search for arbitrary wordcount
numbers of their choice).

column1: Option to NOT restore from draft
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 274
When you create a new work but don't post it, it appears the next time you
click "Post New". It'd be good to give people the option of whether or not
to restore the saved work, though - maybe with a pop-up window similar to
the one on Livejournal. It would probably also be handy to have a "Clear"
button at the bottom of the form that would delete the unposted work and
reload the form. We definitely need at least one of these options ASAP.

(One reason to delete the old work instead of just clearing the fields is
that if you have co-authors on an unposted work, you can't get rid of them.
So under the current system, if I create a draft with someone else as a
co-author and then don't post it, the other person then *can't* post a new
story without me listed as a co-author. That's not good!)

column1: Fandom tags on story entry page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 286
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the revision number next to
"An Archive Of Our Own: Extreme Alpha (rev. #)" in the header).  

unknown - no rev # in header

Please provide any additional information below.

Related to Issue 158

Having the Fandom tags (on story entry pages) be a free form field could be
problematic - both for the database and the users.  Freeform allows for
spelling errors to create multiples of a fandom, or differences in entry of
the fandom (ie: Supernatural/Stargate Atlantis vs. Stargate
Atlantis/Supernatural - this would be 2 entries by fandom, but they're the
same 'fandom').

If there were a dropdown box with a list with 'multiple selection'
available, this would eliminate a lot of these types of errors.  There may
need to be some preliminary selection criteria to make the list more
managable -> TV, Film, Music, Literature, etc., then subcategories,
perhaps?  This dropdown should also be searchable by typing in the letters
for the fandom name, instead of 'scroll only' for ease of use.

There would also need to be an 'other' option to allow for manual entry of
a fandom name that isn't already in the list.  However, this should have a
built in delay and need to be entered manually to the story by an
administrator to avoid duplicating existing fandoms with incorrect
spellings of the fandom name, etc.

Consequently they must be wrapped in block level elements. 2) Forms are structured as definition lists as per the coding standards. A definition list must contain at least one term/definition pair. A definition list can only contain dt/dd pairs directly (first child).
FORM LABEL
INPUT TAG

SUBMIT

A term
may have multiple definitions
. A
must have a term. A list
may have multiple term/definition pairs. 3) Some forms cannot be logically structured as term/definition pairs. These are structured as paragraphs. We may use breaks in these structures, unless you can think of a better option:

INPUT TAG INPUT TAG INPUT TAG FORM LABEL

FORM LABEL
INPUT TAG

SUBMIT

4) All forms must be labelled. It would be great if someone would sort them out with fieldsets and legends, too. A dedicated forms wrangler would be marvellous. Anyone up for the job should check out: http://joeclark.org/book/sashay/serialization/Chapter12.html 5) Forms are styled in the forms.css, which is a work in progress. ==NOTE: The wireframes are very specific about where they want submit buttons and there's no generalisable rule, so I recommend we mark up every submit button with a

13/Feb/09 2:23 PM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;OK, this is not broken, just a tad clumsy, so I'm un-assigning myself from it for

The way it works now is:
- an inspiration link added before first previewing a new work is saved and displayed
in the preview. It can then be removed from the story view page with Remove Relationship.
- a link added on subsequent edit/preview cycles can be edited, removed etc. until
author saves the changes. After this - removal can be done from the story view page.
- adding several inspiration links is therefore fully possible, but only sequentially.
- duplicates are not created anymore. Already created duplicates will have to be
removed manually.

required for safety but is required to protect against breaking the user
interface. 

In the long run, ideally we would allow style attributes through, and
display stories inside a kind of sandbox pane where at the end of it, we
reset everything, which also comes with a button that lets the reading user
strip out all the style attributes (with a preference to always read that
way as well). 

Post-beta feature!

working on some other things at the time and noted that this one was open so I left
the issue alone.

appeared in the story title area.  Draft gave option to post unlike the previous
work. Also, text of work had double dashes and emdashes in the story. These imported
as crazy symbols instead of punctuation.  Posted story (with all import information)
is here: http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/works/6296

number of words/characters.  Some archive header information then imported into the
story.  Story itself did not fully imported, but stopped at a seemingly random
location in the file (after 2181 words).  Draft gave option to post, so I posted the
story as was so the import could be seen.
http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/works/6297

We couldn't save this work, sorry!
Here are the problems we found:
    * Title can't be blank
    * Title must be at least 1 characters long.
The entire post new work page was blank.
After a little thought, I wondered if all of the chapters were public entries.  I
also wondered if this was due to multiple URLs.  I tried again below ---

6) http://amberleewriter.insanejournal.com/56099.html (this time as the only url and
checked to make sure that this was a public entry)
Import worked.  Title imported correctly.  Summary imported correctly (and complete).
 Notes also imported correctly.  All of tags and other info in header of post
imported (but I would expect this with a journal entry so no biggie).  While some
line breaks (spacing with br or p tags) did not import, all italic, blockquotes, and
bold text imported without a problem.  Dashes and emdashes imported correctly and
show up instead of being strange symbols as with the other archive.

Am setting this to "assigned" as test doesn't show that FFNet or livejournal based
code (previous import locations) are necessarily working properly for me.  If coders
feel exact replication is required and would rather work only with previous
tester/feel this is a resolution, please set it back and I'll bug off!  --Amberlee

column98:
20/Sep/08 4:11 PM;557058:573eda1f-b3be-4c7c-8bf0-858526194e9b;Revision 803 is the first pass at the back-end code for account deletion. The text is
still rough - I deviated from the draft wireframes slightly to make things easier
from a coding perspective for now. I also still need to look into separating pseuds
with commas if they're in a list.

There are so many different options involved in the deletion process that I think it
could do with quite vigorous testing. Some things to check:

- If a user has no works, they should be taken straight to the delete confirmation
page
- If a user does have works, a form should be displayed so they can choose what
should happen to the works
- Are the numbers of works listed on the form correct? Are all of the user's pseuds
and co-authors being shown?
- Do all of the options work as they're supposed to? e.g. user's pseud being retained
or replaced, etc.
- Does the form appear correctly if the user has no co-authored works?
- Does it appear correctly if they are only a co-author, and have no fics of their
own where they are the sole author?
- Does it work if they have put more than one of their own pseuds on a fic? Does it
treat that as a solo-authored fic which they can delete if they choose? Does it work
if they have more than one of their pseuds on a fic they are co-authoring with
another user, and does it recognise that it's a co-authored fic which can't be deleted?

I've done my best to test the above locally and it seems to be working for me, but
it
could do with checking.

When a work is deleted, currently only a notification is emailed to the user, not a
copy of the work itself. Do we want the work to be emailed automatically, or should
the user be asked whether they'd like to receive a copy or not?

column99:
17/Sep/08 12:20 PM;557058:37f70620-8e3d-436d-8d7e-e58dca52a891;There's also the whole Pre-slash, pre-whatever angle, too (and the tamer versions of
yaoi and yuri: shounen ai and shoujo ai). But. 

I think the original post above shows that "genre" really doesn't work as a label for
this category. When I think of 'genre,' I think: humor, hurt/comfort, angst, mystery,
adventure, fluff, etc. And that's the textbook definition. Using the term 'genre' to
-only- represent the gender of the romantic pairing... is just plain unconventional
and counter-intuitive. Call it something else. Or, include those other keywords and
have it be a multi-select box.

I understand that somewhere along the line it was conceived that those genres, like
'adventure' and 'mystery' would be put in the Tag field... but those. are. genres.
And they still can be treated as tags... they'll just be called something else in the
intake field.

field, but it will be one of the more heavily used of the optional fields, b/c
readers tend to seek out the 'genre' of fic they prefer.  It will be used a lot for
searches, thus should have additional options, and should be a multi-select box.

Alternatively, if we'd like users to be able to search by both 'genre' and 'pairing
definition' (I can't come up with a good word for that), have a separate section for
each.  One entry field for the genre, using the traditional definition (h/c, humour,
etc), another for the pairing type (gen, het slash, etc).

column98:
01/Nov/08 6:27 PM;557058:6f5727a4-d47a-45b6-8132-04378f742448;Here's some user feedback on the archive!

Archive revision: (rev.907)

Feedback:

Thoughts on the recs section.

As the archive grows, one of the most important features will be the recs
section. Recs help us winnow fanfic. 

Outsiders visiting the archive will likely go to the recs page once they're
daunted by the sheer volume of fic. The recs section is our second gateway.
It is especially important to have a carefully designed recs section
on-site because some authors will mark their stories private. 

1) The recs page must sort by the reccer's name, else it will be useless. 

Readers go to a recs page because of the reputation of the reccer.
Delicious assumes the subject (i.e., tag) is more important than who
bookmarks it. As Isiscolo put it, we look for recs based on those who have
similar tastes to our own. Who recc'd the story is the first thing we look for.

2) Several of the current recs don't have reccers' names at all. 

This makes it seem as though tagging and reccing are separate functions
(since we can't join yet, I can't test it). If that's so, it will quickly
create chaos.

3) We need a separate page that lists only a member's recs.

Listing the recs at the bottom of a user's profile will only work for those
don't write. 90% of reccers also write (a lot). Their recs will be buried.
In some cases, under 100+ fics.

4) We need a count of the number of stories recced next to the reccer's name.

Readers need to easily find the active reccers who put a lot of time into
reccing. We can't qualify how good the recs are, but we can quantify them. 

5) I would like to be able to sort the reccer list by number of recs.

If the listing by reccer looks just like the author listing (only with the
number of recs next to the name), it will still be hard to find the active
reccers. Perhaps we can have something similar to delicious's "popular
bookmarks" feature.

6) We need a very long comment field to describe our recs. 

The best reccers (Seperis, for example, or Regan_v here:
http://regan-v.livejournal.com/60719.html#cutid1) write a paragraph (or
more!) about a story. The primary flaw of delicious is that the comment
field is never designed for recs and is waaaaay too small. I can't test
this feature yet, but all the examples seem short.

Finally:

7) What do we do with Meta Recs? 

Is there a place on the archive for long meta-commentaries that involve
more than one fic? There's my SGA Flavor of the Year:
http://icarusancalion.livejournal.com/583242.html, and I know Regan_v does
them as well, usually on a theme. 

Finally, I'm very impressed you guys are on time and the site is functional
and effective. Good work. 

Sent at: 07:15PM EDT Fri 03 October 2008

column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 499
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the revision number next to
"An Archive Of Our Own: Extreme Alpha (rev. #)" in the header).  
rev 907

We need to add new fields to works (and bookmarks?) for user-facing dates,
perhaps published_at and revised_at, and allow the user to customize these
dates (eg to set published_at to the date when the story was originally put
up when posting an older story) and also to auto-update revised_at (rather
than updated_at) when we change the version of the story. 

We can't use the built-in created_at and updated_at for this because we
want these fields to accurately reflect what they are meant to, which is
when the database entry for the work (or bookmark) has been
created/altered, which is not necessarily going to correspond to when the
content encapsulated in the work has been *meaningfully* created or
altered. EG, any migration on the content of work objects (eg to change
titles to strip out spaces as we had to do pre-rev 907) will change the
updated_at data even though this is strictly for data-cleaning and not the
real content.
column98:
12/Oct/08 2:25 PM;557058:573eda1f-b3be-4c7c-8bf0-858526194e9b;Rev. 925 has the first part of this. Published_at and revised_at datetime fields have
been added to works, and the migration should add them for all existing works. The
current set-up is as follows:

- Published_at can be set on the post new work form (or on the edit form). By default
it is set to today's date. The year select box currently goes back to 1950, I wasn't
sure how far it needed to go back.
- Revised_at can only be set by the user on the edit work form (though changing this
shouldn't be difficult if Design feels it should be on the new form too). It is first
set automatically when a work is created, and is updated when a new chapter is added.
Otherwise, it should only change if the user updates it manually.

I haven't yet changed any filters, sorting, ordering, etc to use the new dates.

The labelling of the fields on the work form could do with Design input, or at least
input from someone who's better at that sort of thing than me, hahaha. :D

Do we definitely want published_at and revised_at fields on bookmarks too?

column104:
15/Oct/08 11:21 AM;557058:573eda1f-b3be-4c7c-8bf0-858526194e9b;When trying this out on testarchive just now, I found that when testarchive seems to
hang on update (I had a couple of times when it was very, very slow), if I click the
stop button in my browser and then try hitting the update button again, the
revised_at date doesn't get set from published_at and so the new date I've set isn't
reflected in the works listing etc. Is there a way we could make that more robust?
Or
is it just due to testarchive being slow?

Also, the more I try this out, the more I think we still really need to find a better
way of handling backdating for multichaptered works - it's okay if you're going back
and editing in a published_at date for a work you've already posted to the Archive,
but if you're trying to backdate as you first post a multichaptered work to the
Archive, it's problematic. As soon as you post the second chapter, the revised_at
date gets reset to today (which we do want) - but there's no way to reset the
revised_at date to the published_at date in order to make the work appear in the
right place on the user works page. Since the revised_at date is now only updated if
you change the published_at date, you'd need to change the published_at date to a
random date, save, and then change it back again. I'm not sure what the solution is,
though, because I agree having a field for the revised_at date on the edit form is
overkill... :S

Samvara, some things which should be tested:
1) When posting a new work which isn't backdated, the date shown on the work blurb
in
the user works list / main works list should be accurate (e.g. 'less than a minute
ago').
2) When posting a new work which is backdated, the date shown on the work blurb
should accurate, and the work sorted accordingly (e.g. if a work is backdated to 2003
and the other works are from 2008, it should be at the bottom of the list when the
user works page is first loaded).
3) When editing an existing work to change the published_at date, the new date should
be saved and should also be reflected in the user works listing.
4) When a new chapter is added to a work, whether the work is backdated or not, the
date shown in the user works listing should be updated to 'less than a minute ago'
and the work should have jumped to the top of the list.
5) The way the dates are displayed in the listing should be "X minutes ago" / "X
hours ago" / "X days ago" up to about 30 days ago, after which the actual date should
be displayed, e.g. "6 Nov. 2003" (not 1893 days ago or whatever).
6) And it shouldn't be possible to set a published_at date in the future, but I've
just seen the update that it still is, so, hmmm. *goes to investigate that now*

inelegantly phrased.

I digress. The point to this defect was to resolve the 'edits not saving' bug which
it has done.

The discussion on "Ambiguity" was mostly on email so I'm putting the
salient points in here.

Samvara > I would ignore this option to be honest. How I think it should
and will work is that if you have an ambiguous tag like "Mark" that could
refer to "Mark Hamill OR "Mark (Battle of the Planets)" then you make
"Mark" a synonym of both of them so searching on "Mark" picks up all
possible Marks.

 - this is about ambiguity between tags in the same Category - both
'Character' tags for example and the synonym relationship will handle them
just fine.

Sidra > At the moment, an ambiguous tag has no special properties beyond
that of other freeform tags. In the future we will want an ambiguous tag to
pop up a message saying something like - sorry, Mark is ambiguous, which
did you mean?. For now, as Samvara points out, you might as well make it a
synonym. The only time you have to make it an ambiguity is if it crosses
categories. For example, Harry Potter is an ambiguity, because it is both a
character and a fandom.

 - this is about cross-Category relationships which we believe will be
relatively rare and need to be able to create synonym relationships as
well. We're going to assume that an ambiguous cross-Category tag (Harry
Potter "Character" and Harry Potter "the books") will contain similar words.

1. For a tag marked 'Ambiguous e.g. /en/tags/Mark/edit add a Synonym drop
down menu that contains all possible tags in the database that contain
similar key words (in this case 'Mark')

===
sarken: FTR, the problem isn't so much the pull request (I don't actually think it
can be simplified much) as the way we want to implement it. The best way to do this
is Javascript, not Ruby, but then we run into the issue of it not being available to
anyone who has disabled JS... which sucks because we would be limiting the availability
of the more accessible list.

The existing tag cloud is much more useful to visual users than people with screen
readers. The tags are in an unordered list and their positions aren't related to how
often they're used, nor is the number of uses listed on the page, so the only way to
tell which tags are used more is by looking at the size of the font, which is not something
a screen reader is going to convey. 

I would argue that we should close the issue for *adding* a tag list option and make
an issue for *switching* to the list view instead (if we wanted to, we could add a
just-for-fun Javascript-required cloud view at a later date). I could update the pull
request pretty easily to switch us to the list version, and taking this approach would
get rid of the messy "um, wtf, why are you abusing Ruby this way" parts of the code.

users, quite frankly, unless you are really keenly interested in Angst and Sexual Content.

<.<

display and adding clearer visual markers by way of improving screenreader support,

is not posted is the "Post" link in the chapter's navigation menu, but the
chapter doesn't appear in the Drafts section.

column97:
20/Sep/09 1:12 PM;557058:573eda1f-b3be-4c7c-8bf0-858526194e9b;Committed in r1469. Quite a few different things here:

- The note re author's summary and tags should appear on the form for works and series.
- For external works, I've added fandom, rating, category, pairing and character
tags. Pending the approval of Content Policy, we've decided not to include warning
tags on external works. Please test everything you can think of here, including:

1) Do tags of all categories save?
2) Tags should not be compulsory, with the exception of fandom - you should be able
to leave them blank.
3) Tag wranglers should, please god, be able to wrangle the tags properly. I am not
well-versed in the tag wrangling side of things and could well have overlooked
something crucial on that front, so I'd appreciate it if the wranglers could take a
good look at that.
4) On the bookmark blurb, icons like for works should now also appear for external
works. If the bookmarker has saved a category or rating, icons should appear for
them. Where warnings would normally be, the external work icon should appear instead.
The proper icon (a blue globe) is still being created, I've used the rec icon as a
placeholder for now so we can check it's working. The final square should always be
blank, as we don't track whether an external work is a WIP or not.

- There should be a note on the bookmarks blurb for external works stating that it's
an external work and information may be incomplete/inaccurate.
- The symbols key, linked from the icons, should have been updated with information
on the new external work icon. That said, for some reason I couldn't get my changes
to show up locally unless I disabled Javascript - I suspect there may be some weird
caching issue going on there...
- If you save a bookmark on an external work, then open up the bookmark form and
paste in the same URL again, if you have Javascript enabled, the previous values for
author, summary, tags etc should be fetched for you automatically. Please check
that's working. Also, if you change any of the fetched values (other than your own
notes and tags), it should save as a bookmark on a new external work, rather than a
bookmark on the existing external work you just created. (You can tell by the 1 on
the little icon on the blurb, rather than 2 or more.) This part was a bit tricky, so
I'd appreciate it if you could check for each of the fields, lovely testers.- **Status changed**: `FixedAndCommited`

meaning rather than alphabetically, and default as following:

Rating should be ordered:

* Not rated

* Teen and up
* Mature
* Explicit

Warnings should be ordered:

    * choose not to warn
    * choose not to warn for some content
    * none of these warnings apply
    * graphic depictions of violence
    * major character death
    * rape/non-con
    * underage

column98:
04/Aug/09 2:23 AM;557058:6f5727a4-d47a-45b6-8132-04378f742448;Good question, I think in that case the user doesn't intend to vanish and would be
sad if they were cut off from their comments.

It should change to their default pseud.
column99:
04/Aug/09 3:03 PM;557058:573eda1f-b3be-4c7c-8bf0-858526194e9b;Committed in r1419.

If a non-default pseud is deleted, its comments should be transferred to the user's
default pseud.
If a user deletes their entire account, all their comments should be shown as
"Account Deleted".
This should apply both to comments on works and comments in inboxes.

There is still a slight potential for Bad Things to happen - if an account is deleted
and its pseud is the last one that has been created site-wide, then when the next
person signs up their default pseud will have the id of the one just deleted - and
they will then own the deleted user's comments. :S That said, this is much, much less

Post Work/Add Chapter

at the end

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 745
What archive revision are you testing on? rev. 1398

Enhance the current user login to put security meassures in place and save
accounts from being easily hacked. Decided on AD&T Meeting 2009/08/29 to
implement as per wiki design:
http://wiki.transformativeworks.org/mediawiki/User_Login_-_AD%26T

1. Limit tries the user has to enter the correct login information to 5 in
2 hours
2. Disable account and IP address from logging in for the next 2 hours
after the 5th try
3. Always (at every step) give the option to reset the password
3.1 If the user follows the link in the email they got sent the account/IP
block will be lifted; not simply when the email is sent
4. Keep the error messages vague and unhelpful, simply "your username or
your password was wrong, please try again" and "you entered the wrong login
data too many times, your account and IP address is temporarily blocked
from logging in"
5. log the account block and the IP address in the user history of the
Admin interface

See the wiki for the exact design and feel free to poke me with any
question you might have. :)

column102:
23/Jan/11 7:29 PM;557058:6f5727a4-d47a-45b6-8132-04378f742448;Comments from a security analyst I met at work :)

The recommended blocking time is a little long. If someone’s trying to log in and fails
( it happens ) then 2 hours will stop them participating. 5 minutes is short enough
to wait around for while the password blocking system resets and will avoid upsetting
members. It’s also sufficient to block most brute-force attacks, since you could have
a 24 hour timeout after three consecutive 5-minute blockouts. 2 hours will push someone
away from their keyboard though. 

As for point 4, the “Username or Password Incorrect.” is good – since it helps to avoid
enumerating the usernames. However you probably want to be told “Warning, your account
will be blocked with X more incorrect attempts” so they don’t just blindly enter the
wrong password five times.  

Keep in mind that as long as permanent damage can’t occur (eg, Deletes can be undone
later) and logging of attempt and accesses are turned on, that security can be fairly
minimal. It’s not like people are storing secret documents in the server. 
 
A bigger issue is that someone might give an account to a friend and the friend will
log in and lock them out. So perhaps having a link to block an account and have an
access evaluated by someone is good to include as well. For dealing with emergency
situations.

Keep in mind that if a friend knows the password, they might also know the email password,
so using email to verify such requests isn’t always possible

column1: IE7 optimisation: Wrong height issues with elements of the Header/Main Navigation in IE7
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 759
What archive revision are you testing on? r1398

Wrong hight issues with elements of the Header/Main Navigation in IE7.

Bing's awesome summary:

1.  The height of the red gradient in the header is too big in IE7 and
therefore goes on into the main content. It should have the same height in
IE7 as in Firefox.

2. The black border with the grey shadow is positioned too low, it should
be positioned so the top of it closes up with the bottom of the navigation
tabs. 


For more information, please also see the wiki page:
http://wiki.transformativeworks.org/mediawiki/Internet_Explorer_7_-_AO3
column97:
22/Sep/09 2:06 AM;557058:293f73e2-2b16-493c-9cc6-61e47ec51fcf;I'd suggest putting the ul id=main-navigation inside a span or a div with
class=main-navigation, for a start. That would make debugging and customising things
like this slightly easier.

The part that is red in IE and white in FF is the margin of the header. Removing the
margin on the header fixes it, though leaves you with less margin. That could be
fixed by increasing the top margin on the main section to compensate. So remove
#header {margin: 0 0 2.5em;} and change #main {margin: 1.5em auto;} to #main {margin:
1.5em auto; margin-top: 2.5em;}
column99:
23/Sep/09 11:37 AM;557058:293f73e2-2b16-493c-9cc6-61e47ec51fcf;The margin thing didn't fix it. I've now found out a little more. In Firefox, if you
change your font size, the size of the header background image remains constant - it
either crops off the bottom, or adds more red background below. In IE, the background
image is stretched to match header+margin. I still can't find what's causing that
margin in IE, though. However, I wonder if we want to think about changing the
behaviour in FF anyway, as it doesn't look good at very large font sizes, which is
an
accessibility issue.

column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 762
**What archive revision are you testing on? 

Right now - Test archive revision #1453 on a PC running Windows XP
Professional 2002 service pack 3 using Firefox v. 3.5.2 

When original problem happened I was on BETA. I am unsure what revision was
applied at that time (It happened on two different days -- August 1st and
August 4th).  I was using both a PC running Windows XP Professional 2002
service pack 3 using Firefox v. 3.5.2 and also on MacOS X.5.8 with Firefox
2.0.0.20  (Yes, I know, very bad tester person for letting this go for so
long.  This will not happen again.)


**What steps will reproduce the problem?

1.After creating a new story with multiple chapters (Echo) I opened it in
"Edit" and attempted to make it a part of a series.  
 
2. I did not have a previously created series, so I entered the new series
name in the field (Emergence Cycle).  

3. I previewed and updated the story.  There was no error.

4. I did not see the series show up in my "series" area but the name of the
series did apply to the story information.  

5. On the story page, I clicked on "Emergence Cycle" and it took me to the
series page for the new series.  I thought, at the time, that it might take
a little time to update or something so I didn't note if the author field
had been filled in.

6.  I waited a few days and tried to attach a second story to this series
(Match).  I opened this story in "edit," selected the "series" option and
the series did not show up as a drop down option.  However, I did not know
if the entry field should have such a function so was uncertain if there
was something wrong. 

7. I went back to the other story attached to the series (Echo) and went
into "edit" mode.  I noted that the name of the series showed up UNDER the
entry field with a "remove" and a "delete" option.  

8.  I went back to the second story (Match) in "edit" and checked to see if
this information showed up under the entry field.  It did not.

9.  I then entered the series name into the available field in the series
area thinking that entering this information again would pull it from the
database or somesuch. 

10. I previewed and accepted the edits.  There was no error.

11. Once again, no series showed up in my series area.  I went to the
second story (Match) and viewed the story.  Again "Emergence Cycle" was
listed.  I thought I had success.  I clicked on "Emergence Cycle" and it
moved me to the series area for this series.

12. Instead of showing two stories, it listed only one (the second story,
Match) as associated with Emergence Cycle.  I was confused and went back to
the previous story (Echo).  Sure enough, it still had "Emergence Cycle"
listed. I clicked on it and went to the series page it showed only one
story -- ECHO?!

13.  So, it seems that I have managed to create two series with exactly the
same name.  Also, they are only associating with a single story.

14. Attempting to delete or remove these unseen series gives a dialogue box
of "Are you sure?" followed by a load of the series page with a pink banner
reading "Sorry, you don't have permission to access the page you were
trying to reach." I tried this on Beta off and on for several weeks and
tried today on TEST

15.  At the suggestion of sarkymoocow I checked each of these series pages.
 Neither has an author associated in the "author" field on the series page.

16. Also at the suggestion of sarkymoocow I checked the series index page.
 "Emergence Cycle" does show up here -- twice.  Once for each story.

16.  This originally happened on BETA.  I checked for series problems in
open issues to see if someone had reported this (as I suck and did not) but
did not see a similar problem.  I did, however, find others.  So I...

17. Created a new story on TEST (today v.1453), added a series, left the
story in draft, and found that I did manage to make a series associated
with my ID/Pseud.  All went fine!  

18.  I then created another new story and associated it with the new test
series without error.  I still, however, can't manage to get the other
stories to disassociate with the orphan series and can't find a way to link
the series to me.


**What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

I expected to get a series listed in my author series area and to be able
to attach multiple stories to this series.  So far, I just keep making the
same series name over and over and it seems to not be associating with my
name at all.

I also did not know what to expect from the series area initially.  I was
unaware that the entry box would have a drop-down option to select the
series on other stories if the series was properly made.  Because of the
malfunction, I saw only the name of the series UNDER this field and thought
that this was were I would select this information in another story to
associate it with the series.  As a result, the experience of both creating
and associating a series was confused for me initially.  Now that I have
managed to do this correctly once, it make perfect sense, but having the
entry field become or be a drop box later might also confuse other users of
the archive.


**Please provide any additional information below.

column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 764
What archive revision are you testing on? r1453

I think this is probably a separate issue again from issue 762. :(

1. Go to post new work. Specify a new series, and preview in order to
create a draft.
2. Go to user series page; see the empty series there.
3. After one week, the draft is automatically deleted. Alternatively, edit
the draft and delete it manually. (In fact, the same applies for posted
works, if it is the only one in the series.)

When a work is deleted we don't want to always destroy any series
associated with it, since the series might contain other works. But if it
was the only work in the series, we should really destroy the series at the
same time.

We should probably also run a data-munging rake task to delete existing
empty series.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 765
Found on Test r1453

What steps will reproduce the problem?

1. Go to edit an unwrangled, uncapitalized tag:
(e.g. http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/airplane/edit )

2. Check "This is the official name for the Freeform" AND Rename the tag to
correct the capitalization (e.g. change "airplane" to "Airplane")

3. Click "Save changes"

The updated tag "Airplane" will appear with the synonym "Airplane".

For example:

http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/Aliens/edit

Has the synonym "Aliens".  If you go to:

http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/Aliens/

The tag is marked with the same links normally seen on a synonym:

"This tag has been merged into Aliens for filtering.
Works tagged with this tag will show up in Aliens's filter.
Bookmarks tagged with this tag will show up in Aliens's filter."

as well as the standard canonical ("common tag") links. (Going to any of
the "Aliens" links brings you to the same "Aliens" tag; it's only one tag,
apparently; it just thinks that it's two.)

If you do the steps separately ("Rename" to correct the capitalization,
save changes, then make canonical and save), it works fine, with no
duplicate synonym created:
http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/Backrub/edit
Renaming and canonizing simultaneously causes the problem.

Note: There are several of these ghost-doubled tags on the Beta archive, as
I didn't realize it was doing it for a time.

column114:
08/Dec/09 2:30 AM;557058:3564dbfd-03c5-46c9-9e5c-3219aea344c7;Sorry to be a downer!

This is not a good solution. This is squashing a fly on a window with a sledgehammer.
Dismantling the fundamental structure of the XHTML framework to fix a small layout
bug is not a productive or constructive approach. 

It's important for all lists to be coded as lists. It's not good enough for it to
look right. It has to be coded correctly and semantically. An unordered list can be
navigated with multiple access technologies; a screenreader, for example, might have
to now read through every link from the beginning every time, instead of being able
to jump directly to link four. A voice-activated navigation system will have to now
tab through the links (unless it's got mouseless browsing on FF3, but that's edge).

With your agreement I will revert every instance to a navigation list. - **Labels added**: Priority-Critical
- **Labels removed**: Priority-Medium
column115:
08/Dec/09 2:42 AM;557058:293f73e2-2b16-493c-9cc6-61e47ec51fcf;The change from lists was originally due to problems with the main navigation in IE7.

it
back. I agree that it's not ideal, but I couldn't find any other way to fix it, and
the main nav thing (which prompted this change) was really urgent for Open Beta.
However, this one is mainly cosmetic, so we could revert this change and leave the
main nav, given that this one is also going to affect screenreaders and is less
important for IE7. (And thanks for explaining why about the lists thing. I knew it
was supposedly better design, but no-one had actually explained why before.)

external works has been added. It's made the form a bit bulky and

the form is draggable. Suggestions made in AD&T include a drop shadow - the
lovely Bingeling is planning to add them to the wiki, I'll update this
issue with a link once it's up. :)

column1: Users and People have unnecessary duplication
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 792
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the revision number next to
"An Archive Of Our Own: Extreme Alpha (rev. #)" in the header).

r1531

This is a code design issue rather than a front-end issue but involves some
design input. 

Currently, people is very nearly just a duplicate of the users index which
is a problem because it violates "Don't Repeat Yourself" principles and
will inevitably lead to inconsistency. 

Solutions:


1) Have users index just redirect to people index and get rid of the users
index views. This still splits off people controller/views without an
underlying principle and doesn't feel intuitive, but on the upside it is
quick and easy and keeps the "people" url. We shouldn't really have the
people url if we're keeping to a clean RESTful design -- that is,
("people/[name]" should be the person you look at going from the "people/"
index, not "people/" => "users/[name]"). However, because people/ includes
pseuds also, there's a case to be made for stepping outside this for the
index. 

-- OR --

1) Get rid of the duplicate people controller/views and just keep users
including pseuds (as it already does). 

2) If necessary, rename users to people --> this is a huge amount of work
for a fairly tiny reward IMO, just having "people" versus "users" in the
urls, but if we are going to do it, we should do it now before too many
users have shared the URLs to their archive home pages. The downside is
this would break any existing users' links to their archive home pages.

column1: Matching data across external bookmarks to the same link
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 811
As per issue 707 : when an external bookmark is posted with a link already
in the archive, data from the previous bookmark is automatically fetched. 
If the information is left untouched, then the bookmark will post as a
second bookmark on the link (with a "2" beside it).

Adding or changing any of this top-level info (title, author, summary,
tags) makes a new bookmark.  However, the top-level info is always fetched
from the first external bookmark made.  If you alter that info, then it
saves as a new bookmark (even if you change it to the same info as another
bookmark.) So if one user made a bookmark with only a little top-level
info, then any other user who bookmarks that link who adds any top-level
info, will be making a new bookmark, even if other users have made
bookmarks with the identical info.  Somehow bookmarks for the same links
will need to be synched or organized.

03/Dec/09 9:31 PM;557058:9bc483b7-178b-4f29-87d3-3e1e7fb3dda9;IN SHORT: This seems to work (mostly) right on Firefox, but I'd like if someone else tested this again. There are a couple bugs both on Chrome and IE. On Firefox, the "Filter these works" title on the filter menu should be fixed so it wraps and don't extend outside of the gray background when the browser's size is reduced; similarly, the "Filter works" button's alignment should be fixed so it doesn't extends so much outside of the menu's gray background when the browser's size is reduced. Tested on: Browsers >> Firefox 3.5.5, Chrome 3.0.195.33, IE 8.0.6001.18828 Screen resolutions >> 800 x 600, 1024 x 768, 1280 x 800 Pages >> Homepage (logged-in & logged-out), My Home, an specific work page, Works, Fandoms, People, Bookmarks, Tags Results: When the browsers windows are maximized, the different elements flex properly: no boxes, text or image overlaps. As the windows' sizes are reduced, most elements move and align as to prevent overlaps -- exceptions are: ON CHROME # on the homepage (both logged-in & logged out), the searchbox overlaps the "Archive of Our Own" title -- it looks fine in the rest of the site; # whenever there's a list of works, the works titles either a) move to the right of the warnings/pairings square image (they should stay under the square image) or b) move way down, so the user has to scroll a longer distance than with the other two browsers; # whenever there's a list of works, the works dates move in ways they shouldn't -- they overlap the works titles, overlap the warnings/pairings square image, or move really close to it (then they should align to the left); # whenever there's a "Filter these results" menu, when the browser window is reduced to certain size (1/3 of the screen or smaller, at any resolution), the text in the filtering menu overlaps the menu's gray background box and the help sign ('?') is pushed out of the gray box. ON IE # on the homepage (both logged-in & logged out), the searchbox overlaps the "Archive of Our Own" title -- it looks fine in the rest of the site; # whenever there's a list of works, the works dates move in ways they shouldn't -- they overlap the warnings/pairings square image, or move really close to it (then they should align to the left); # whenever there's a "Filter these results" menu, when the browser window is reduced to certain size (1/3 of the screen or smaller, at any resolution), the menu's title overlaps the gray background box; # certain images/backgrounds show straight corners instead of the rounded ones in Firefos and Chrome -- for example, in the homepage, and on the help image ("?"). ON FIREFOX I need somebody else to test this browser again, as on my side the results are definitely not what I expected: once the browser's width had been reduced to about one third of the screen (people that multitask might do this), the flexible layout stopped working (even if it still worked for IE and Chrome at the same width), and horizontal scrolling (or even maximizing the window and/or reducing the font size) was needed to navigate the site. (I wonder if this is a problem with my browser, as I'm using a portable version and a similar problem occurs when navigating other webpages) Nonetheless, at a slightly wider width, the flexibility of the layout works right, except for the title on the filtering menu (which overlaps the menu's gray background) AND the "Filter Works" button, which moves to the right. 09/Nov/09 2:12 PM;557058:6ed4cad3-fb18-4d8a-9718-c1cc381e0d61;Mac OX 10.5 has a known issue with Gecko-based browsers not correctly displaying
Cyrillic fonts in drop-down lists, though they're fine in Web pages themselves,
unless you're using the Russian (or other Cyrillic, I assume) interface for the OS.
This can be hacked using Stylish or UserContent.css to add

select {
font-family: 'Lucida Grande' !important;
}

Devanagari scripts don't show up in the dropdown for me, either, though the hack
doesn't fix it and I haven't been able to find one that does.

All fonts display fine in Safari on 10.5, however. The report I found specifically
mentioned 10.5, so other versions of OSX may or may not be affected.

Other testers, please report what you see for your OS before we mark this confirmed.
Thanks!

column1: Bookmarks on external works created before bookmarks upgrade can't be edited due to lack of fandom tag
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 910
What archive revision are you testing on? r1692

See also support issue #215 on 16bugs
(https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/121540).

External works created via bookmarks before the bookmarks upgrade have no
fandom tag. We've now made fandom a required tag. An unfortunate
side-effect is that bookmarks on external works created before the upgrade
can no longer be edited. Because the tag should be on the external work
rather than the bookmark, the user can't add it; at the same time, they
can't save the bookmark because the tag is missing. :(

This needs consideration by AD&T (I'll add it to an agenda in the near
future), but my initial suggestion would be that we create an interface to
allow admins to edit external works (I think that would be good for other
reasons too). Then we would have to go through and add the correct fandoms
to the external works without them. I realise that's not ideal, but there
shouldn't be too many, external works were a bit hidden.

regardless of whether they have a media or fandom checked.

column100:
18/Nov/09 3:40 PM;557058:56c6aaf0-abec-4140-88a3-59aa2f24c990;Hi, ars.arboreous!

Thought I'd jump in here and try to make sense of this - it's a tag wrangling issue,
and kind of complicated.  Basically, the associations between a pairing and
characters doesn't happen automatically - the system doesn't automatically tie
together "Bob Bryar" with "Bob Bryar/Frank Iero"; instead, one of us tag wranglers
goes to the pairing and manually adds in the two characters.  So with Bob/Gerard, the
system doesn't tie that pairing to any or all "Bob"s in the archive; instead a
wrangler decides which Bob the pairing applies to, and ties it to that Bob ("Bob
Bryar", in this case).

Once the character is tied to the pairing, then only the pairing, not the character,
is displayed on the "works" page (since Bob Bryar/Gerard Way, Bob Bryar, Gerard Way
looks redundant).  The fic is still tagged with that character - if you filter by
character: "Bob Bryar", your Bob/Gerard fic should still come up, even if the
character isn't showing; and if you go read the fic itself, "Bob Bryar" should be
listed in the character tags at the top of the page. (Whatever wranglers do, we
shouldn't be altering any of your actual tags, just how they're organized.)

If you have other fics where the pairing and characters are both listed on the works
page, then that's probably because the tag wranglers haven't gotten around to hooking
up those pairings with those characters - with the archive newly opened and all the
new pairings and characters added, we're behind on our wrangling.  Eventually, all
the pairings and characters will be associated, but it'll take a little while.

So that's what's going on with your tags. If you have any more questions, please ask.
 And thank you for the feedback - and never worry if it's not what we're looking for;
we're looking for everything! You're not the only person who's been confused by the
pairing/character display, so that's definitely something we need to explain better,
and it's very helpful for us to know this. :)

X-parrot
Tag Wrangling Subcommittee

column1: Prioritizing of duplicate tags
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 945
r1742

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Post a new work with new duplicate tags in more than one field: E.g.
"Testing Taggy" in both the Fandom and the Freeform tag field.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Because the system cannot handle having duplicate tags, the tag in "Fandom"
is renamed "Testing Taggy - Fandom". See:
http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/works/15976

This then causes trouble for the tag wranglers, who have to get an admin to
rename the fandom Testing Taggy to "Testing Taggy" and name the freeform
tag to "Testing Taggy - Freeform"

Ideally, when the system is presented with two new duplicate tags
simultaneously, it would prioritize the non-freeform tag.  So, given a
conflicting identical tag in the Fandom, Pairing, or Character field, the
freeform would be renamed "- Freeform" and the Fandom/Pairing/Char tag
would be left as-is.  Basically, we want the posting interface to process
the Fandom/Pairing/Char tag fields before it processes the Freeform field.

(Actually ideally users wouldn't be entering duplicate tags, but at present
it's pretty easy to get confused - renaming the Tags field will hopefully
help with that, but until then, it would be really helpful for us wranglers
if we didn't have to be renaming all the duplicates.)

(Um, and I'm not a coder, so if what we're requesting doesn't make sense,
please ask me to clarify!)

ids[0...ArchiveConfig.SPHINX_FILTER_SIZE_LIMIT] instead of '-1' would work.

31/May/12 3:57 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Users with JS disabled aren't going to be able to show/hide warnings unless we implement
a backend solution that causes the page to refresh, which I suspect is something we
want to avoid. The best solution here is to hide the non-functional 'Show warnings'
link from JS users* and clarify that the preference only works when JS is disabled.

*The way to do this is style the 'Show warnings' link with display: none by default
and then use Javascript to change it to display: inline (or change/remove the class
that applies display: none; it doesn't particularly matter how we do it). That way,
users with JS disabled won't see a non-functional option, but users with JS enabled
will see it.

column1: Feature: importing works for other users
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 983
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the revision number next to
"An Archive Of Our Own: Extreme Alpha (rev. #)" in the header).

revision 1775

IMPORTANT NOTE: this relies on being able to parse author information from
whatever source we are importing. Currently that only works for
livejournal, and IF the livejournal's user profile shows their email
address to non-logged-in users. (This will soon be broadened, but for now
just test only by importing from LJ.)

Here's the expected behavior:

- An archivist is a user who is marked as an archivist by admins (same way
that users get made into tag wranglers or translators).

- An archivist who looks at the import form can import more works at once
and can import works for other users. 

- When works for other users are imported, we try and work out the identity
of the user from the source (as noted above, right now this is only working
for livejournal, if the user has their email displayed on their profile). 

- If we can do so, we go down one of two paths:

PATH ONE: Either there is a user in the archive who is already using this
email address as the address on their profile, or there is a user in the
archive who has already claimed this email address previously. 

* The user will automatically be given ownership of the stories in question.
* The user will be sent an email notification that the stories were added
to her account. 


PATH TWO: There is no user in the archive who has claimed this email address. 

* The user will receive an invitation email explaining about the import
process, with a link to claim their works. 

* If the user already has an account, they can log in and claim the stories
into their existing account. 

* The user can also create a new account, and when it is activated, the
stories will be added to their new account.

* If the user claims the stories, she will be sent an email notification
that the stories were added to her account. 

* The user can also instead orphan or delete the works if they wish.

Archivists can now import for other people. In order to avoid the
notifications annoying people, we want to allow users to specify if they
don't want to be emailed and if they don't want their works imported. 

* If someone either comes from an invitation or edits the settings for an
external author they have already claimed at /[user]/external_authors, and
chooses "do not import", if an archivist attempts to import from the same
account again, they should get an error message that the user has barred
importing. 

* If someone chooses "do not email", then when works are imported from the
same email address, they should not get notifications. They SHOULD still be
assigned the works if they have an archive account.

revision 1781

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Try importing failed works into the story importer.
2. Error messages will be a mess. :)

This requires a general refactoring of the handling of errors in the story
import process; FWIW the difficulty is that because we are handling batches
of works, and the batch processing has been moved into the story parser
model out of the works controller, it is now a little trickier to provide
appropriate error messages in the controller. 

This should be done by creating some custom error classes in StoryParser
and returning an array of these, which can then be checked in the works
controller where a clean, translateable error message can then be returned
to the user.

Something very bad is going on here - I think what's happening is that the
code assumes a fandom will only have a single media tag, and when that's
not the case, you bounce endlessly between the add_media and wrangle_parent
methods. We should make it not do that!
